newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco signs $500 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Codelco signs $500 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco signed a $500 million loan with 18 North American, European and Japanese banks, the company said in a statement.

The loan, whose basic terms were announced September 10, was signed in New York by Codelco officials Mario Espinoza and Jos Antonio Alvarez, plus representatives of the banks, said Codelco in a statement.

The statement gave the first complete list of banks involved in the loan. The banks acting as lead managers are Citibank, Banca Commerciale Italiana, Canadian Imperial Bank and Bank of Montreal, said Codelco.
The loan's managers are Bank of Tokyo, Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, Fuji Bank Limited, Union Bank of Switzerland, Caja Madrid, Banca Monte del Paschi di Siena.

With Chase Manhattan Bank acting as principal agent, the banks committing $50 million each to the loan are The Royal Bank of Canada, JP Morgan, Bank of America, Banque Nationale de Paris, Industrial Bank of Japan, Internationale Nederlanden Bank N.V. and Banco Exterior Espaa, said the statement.
With an interest rate of 0.22 percent over Libor, the loan will be used to pay for a series of expansion plans at Codelco, company officials said last month without giving details.
Codelco's main projects currently include construction of the Radomiro Tomic mine in northern Chile and expansion at the Andina mine near Santiago.
